name: r2-across-2
statement: The RL-Zero-Math delta is small (0.24 % of weight norm) and sign-coherent: its function lies in the joint sign pattern of many coordinates, whose Fisher curvature on the base's own math samples is hundreds to thousands of times that of a random direction of the same norm, not in its large entries. So the effect of any edit is its energy divided by that leverage. Random resampling (DARE), random-sign or random-direction edits of the same norm, and magnitude-ranked subsets add almost nothing beyond their unbiased share of the sign pattern. The model's activations on general text barely move. The dose curve stays near-linear past a = 1. DARE fails only when its noise energy (1-q)/q exceeds the leverage, which puts the cliff at q of about 0.01-0.05 %. A large, low-coherence SFT delta (bytegraft, Think-SFT) fails all of these tests.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math delta (MLP and full), partial and resampled copies of it, base + a*(RL - base) for a in [0, 1.5], and teacher-forced KL and activation readouts. MATH-500 at the n13 setting (T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, plain) and at T 1.0 with the cue, grader v3. Contrasted with SFT deltas (Bolmo-1B bytegraft, Olmo-3 Think-SFT). Revises r1-surprises-2: the bytegraft result (DARE gives 0/1,200 on an SFT delta that a rank-1 LoRA can fit) shows that low-rank structure alone does not decide DARE tolerance; the sign coherence relative to the delta's size does. Does not cover the sampling-temperature results or which behaviours (format, length) the delta encodes.

imports.finding: For Olmo-3-7B RL-Zero deltas, Fisher curvature along the RL direction is ~708x (388-1,508) that of a random same-norm direction; the effect sits in signs and cross-coordinate structure (sign-flip null loses most, magnitude alignment ~1); DARE damage follows (1-p)/(p*rho_sign) of the delta's own KL, and SFT-like deltas with rho_sign < 6 fail by keep 0.1.
imports.how: Turns the team's flat DARE curve (85.2-87.8 for q = 0.1-3 %) into a lower bound on leverage (above ~1,500 for the 3.1 MLP delta) and predicts a cliff below q = 0.05 %, a sign-flipped delta at base level, a sign-only delta at RL level, and a random direction needing ~30-55x RL's norm to match RL's KL.

imports.finding: DARE's output error is bounded by the drop rate and by the mean and variance of delta-times-activation; large deltas (MetaMath-7B, mean |delta| 0.017) break already at drop rate 0.1, small ones survive.
imports.how: Explains why the same DARE copy that works on the 0.24 %-norm RL delta gives 0/1,200 on the bytegraft SFT delta, and predicts DARE at 1 % on the 24.8 %-norm Think-SFT delta degenerates.

imports.finding: For a small alignment delta the reward is first-order linear along theta_0 + gamma*delta, so extrapolating past gamma = 1 helps or holds until the delta is large.
imports.how: With the RL delta 100x smaller than the SFT delta and first-order linear in KL (0.542 predicted vs 0.549 measured), predicts base + 1.5*(RL - base) holds at RL level, unlike the bytegraft SFT dose curve that collapses past 1.1.

explains.how: DARE keeps the expected sign pattern; its noise, being random-direction, carries 1/leverage of the KL per unit energy, so even 1,000x energy costs little.

explains.quote: DARE's realized change energy is 33 to 1,000 times the whole delta's
explains.how: Flat accuracy at 1,000x noise energy means the leverage exceeds ~1,000, which places the DARE cliff just below q = 0.1 %.

explains.quote: matched on change energy (two kinds) 58.0-63.8: H_local REFUTED
explains.how: Magnitude carries no extra function (alignment ~1), so the most-changed neurons act like random ones of equal energy.
Each subset closes about its share of the coherent pattern; ranking by weight change finds no special support.

explains.quote: summed first-order scores predict a 0.542-nat drop
explains.how: A small coherent delta acts in the first-order regime, so pieces add linearly and the dose curve stays linear past a = 1.
The two RL runs share the base-set update mask but their sign patterns are independent, and the function lies in the sign pattern, so the two deltas are orthogonal in function.
Most entries are tiny; the function cannot sit in large entries, only in coherent signs across many coordinates.

explains.quote: the imitation delta (24.8% of norm, 100x larger) does not point along RL
explains.how: The SFT delta is large and of low coherence, the regime where DARE and extrapolation fail.
An SFT delta with low sign coherence cannot survive 1,000x random noise energy, where the RL delta does.

explains.quote: Peak at lambda 0.7-0.8, not 1; past 1.1 the model collapses
explains.how: A large SFT delta leaves the first-order regime before lambda = 1; the small RL delta should not.

explains.quote: the RL change is 11-27x smaller per band
explains.how: The delta's leverage is concentrated on the base's own math samples, so on general text it moves top contexts only a little.
General-text curvature along the delta is low, so general-text activations stay at r 0.9986-0.9997 while math-text outputs change.

explains.quote: Mean KL per token after the cue 0.06-0.09 nats
explains.how: A delta of 0.24 % norm produces 0.06-0.09 nats per token only because its leverage is high; a random direction of the same norm would give about a thousandth of it.

conflicts.quote: a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain
conflicts.how: On Qwen3.5-0.8B a random edit of matched norm gave most of the gain; the theory must hold that this happens only on a 95 %-cap-hit model, where any perturbation helps, and not on Olmo at T 1.0.

conflicts.quote: DARE (each MLP delta entry kept with prob q = 0.1-3 %
conflicts.how: The published law with rho ~708 predicts that DARE at q = 0.1 % loses about 140 % of the delta's KL, yet accuracy stays at 85.2, so the 3.1 MLP delta needs leverage above ~1,500 or accuracy must saturate in KL. Either way the published constant does not fit as-is.

conflicts.quote: 11.8% of its squared norm sits in 8 singular directions per matrix
conflicts.how: A low-rank energy head 15-20x above null suggests magnitude structure carries information, against the claim that the function is in the signs alone.
Weight-change ranking closes ~5x more KL than random at 1 %, more than its 1.5 % energy share, so magnitude is not fully uninformative.

rival: Low-rank function plus high-rank noise (r1-surprises-2): DARE works because the few top singular directions per matrix survive resampling in expectation, while the noise is high-rank and harmless. Separation: (1) a sign-only delta, sign(delta) times each matrix's RMS |delta|, which flattens the singular spectrum the rival relies on and turns the 54 % sub-ulp entries into full-size entries: this theory predicts RL-level accuracy, the rival predicts a large loss; (2) DARE at q = 0.01 %: the noise is still high-rank, so the rival predicts it stays near 85, while this theory predicts a cliff because the noise energy (~10,000x) exceeds the leverage.

predictions.experiment: DARE on the MLP delta only, keep q = 0.01 % (scale 10,000), attention and norms base, plain prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, one sample, cap 16,384, grader v3 (MLP-only arm ~86.4 % under v1)
predictions.refuted_by: 425 or more right (no cliff: DARE stays flat at 10,000x noise energy)

predictions.experiment: Sign-flipped delta: base + |RL - base| with each entry's sign drawn at random (all tensors), opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 430 or more right (magnitudes without RL's signs carry the gain)

predictions.experiment: Sign-only delta: base + sign(RL - base) * (per-matrix RMS of the nonzero |RL - base| entries), zero entries stay zero, all tensors, opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 420 right (the magnitudes, not the signs, carry the function)

predictions.experiment: base + 1.5*(RL - base), all tensors, opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: right (with cap hits expected at most 35)
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 435 right or more than 50 cap hits (the RL delta leaves the linear regime by 1.5 like the bytegraft SFT delta)

predictions.experiment: Random direction per matrix with Frobenius norm 30x that matrix's RL delta: teacher-forced mean KL(edited || base) per token on RL's 500 T 1.0 MATH-500 answers after the cue (RL's own KL to base is 0.06-0.09)
predictions.refuted_by: 0.07 or more (leverage below ~900, so the flat DARE curve is unexplained)

predictions.experiment: DARE keep q = 1 % (scale 100) of the Olmo-3-7B-Think-SFT minus base delta on transformer body tensors only (embeddings and lm_head base), plain prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 150 or more right (a large, low-coherence SFT delta survives DARE)
